istem:
Research question: Yapay zeka kod üretim modellerinin ürettiği koddaki hata türleri ve kalite sorunları üzerine en önemli çalışmalar ve açık problemler neler?

Cutoff date: 2025-11-04. Only works published BEFORE this date count.

List the 30 most important works (papers) for this research question that were published before the cutoff date, in order of importance (most important first), each with its arXiv id and/or DOI. You may search the web.

When you are done, reply with ONLY a JSON object in this form (no other text):
{"calismalar": [{"sira": 1, "baslik": "exact title", "yil": 2020, "arxiv_id": "arXiv id or null", "doi": "DOI or null", "gerekce": "one sentence on why this work is important"}]}
with exactly 30 items. If you do not know an identifier, use null instead of guessing.

calismalar.baslik: Asleep at the Keyboard? Assessing the Security of GitHub Copilot's Code Contributions
calismalar.gerekce: This is the first systematic study of security flaws in code produced by an AI assistant: it tested CWE-based scenarios and found about 40% of Copilot's code was vulnerable.

calismalar.baslik: Is Your Code Generated by ChatGPT Really Correct? Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation
calismalar.gerekce: EvalPlus showed that weak test suites hide wrong code, and that measured pass@k drops sharply once tests are made more rigorous.

calismalar.baslik: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
calismalar.gerekce: Codex and HumanEval set the standard for functional-correctness evaluation, and the paper gives an early analysis of the limits and risks of generated code.

calismalar.baslik: Towards Understanding the Characteristics of Code Generation Errors Made by Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It builds a detailed taxonomy of semantic and syntactic errors that LLMs make in code generation (ICSE 2025).

calismalar.baslik: What's Wrong with Your Code Generated by Large Language Models? An Extensive Study
calismalar.gerekce: This large-scale study classifies bugs in LLM-generated code and analyzes them by type and root cause.

calismalar.baslik: Bugs in Large Language Models Generated Code: An Empirical Study
calismalar.gerekce: It proposes a taxonomy of bug patterns specific to LLM-generated code (e.g., misinterpretation, hallucinated objects) and validates it with a practitioner survey.

calismalar.baslik: Refining ChatGPT-Generated Code: Characterizing and Mitigating Code Quality Issues
calismalar.gerekce: It characterizes the correctness and maintainability problems in ChatGPT's code and tests how well these problems can be fixed through conversation.

calismalar.baslik: No Need to Lift a Finger Anymore? Assessing the Quality of Code Generation by ChatGPT
calismalar.gerekce: It evaluates ChatGPT's code for correctness, complexity and security across many tasks, and studies how quality changes over time.

calismalar.baslik: Do Users Write More Insecure Code with AI Assistants?
calismalar.gerekce: This user study (CCS 2023) found that developers with AI assistance wrote less secure code while being more confident that it was secure.

calismalar.baslik: Lost at C: A User Study on the Security Implications of Large Language Model Code Assistants
calismalar.gerekce: This controlled user study measures how LLM assistants affect the rate of security bugs in C code.

calismalar.baslik: Is GitHub's Copilot as Bad as Humans at Introducing Vulnerabilities in Code?
calismalar.gerekce: It compares Copilot with human developers on whether they reproduce known real-world vulnerabilities.

calismalar.baslik: Security Weaknesses of Copilot Generated Code in GitHub
calismalar.gerekce: It analyzes the CWE distribution of AI-generated code found in real GitHub projects.

calismalar.baslik: LLM Hallucinations in Practical Code Generation: Phenomena, Mechanism, and Mitigation
calismalar.gerekce: It classifies the types and causes of code hallucinations in repository-level, real-world tasks.

calismalar.baslik: Exploring and Evaluating Hallucinations in LLM-Powered Code Generation
calismalar.gerekce: It builds a taxonomy of code hallucinations and the HalluCode benchmark.

calismalar.baslik: CodeHalu: Investigating Code Hallucinations in LLMs via Execution-based Verification
calismalar.gerekce: It defines and measures code hallucination types by verifying them through execution.

calismalar.baslik: We Have a Package for You! A Comprehensive Analysis of Package Hallucinations by Code Generating LLMs
calismalar.gerekce: It measures at large scale how LLMs invent nonexistent packages, and the supply-chain risk this creates (slopsquatting).

calismalar.baslik: An Empirical Evaluation of GitHub Copilot's Code Suggestions
calismalar.gerekce: This early empirical study (MSR 2022) measures the correctness and understandability of Copilot's suggestions across languages.

calismalar.baslik: Evaluating the Code Quality of AI-Assisted Code Generation Tools: An Empirical Study on GitHub Copilot, Amazon CodeWhisperer, and ChatGPT
calismalar.gerekce: It compares the validity, correctness, reliability and maintainability of code from three assistants, including code smells.

calismalar.baslik: How Secure is Code Generated by ChatGPT?
calismalar.gerekce: It shows that ChatGPT often produces vulnerable code across multiple languages and only fixes it when explicitly asked.

calismalar.baslik: Purple Llama CyberSecEval: A Secure Coding Benchmark for Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It is a large-scale benchmark that measures how often LLMs suggest insecure code.

calismalar.baslik: Large Language Models for Code: Security Hardening and Adversarial Testing
calismalar.gerekce: SVEN shows that the security of generated code can be controlled, and it set the evaluation protocol for this problem.

calismalar.baslik: CWEval: Outcome-driven Evaluation on Functionality and Security of LLM Code Generation
calismalar.gerekce: It evaluates functional correctness and security together, showing that code can be correct yet insecure.

calismalar.baslik: BaxBench: Can LLMs Generate Correct and Secure Backends?
calismalar.gerekce: It shows that even the strongest models produce many exploitable vulnerabilities when generating realistic backend applications.

calismalar.baslik: Is Self-Repair a Silver Bullet for Code Generation?
calismalar.gerekce: It shows that models' ability to find and fix their own errors is limited, an important open problem.

calismalar.baslik: Beyond Functional Correctness: Investigating Coding Style Inconsistencies in Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It builds a taxonomy of style and readability inconsistencies in LLM-generated code.

calismalar.baslik: An Empirical Study of Code Smells in Transformer-based Code Generation Techniques
calismalar.gerekce: It shows that code smells in the training data carry over into the code that models generate.

calismalar.baslik: An Empirical Study of the Non-determinism of ChatGPT in Code Generation
calismalar.gerekce: It shows that the same prompt can yield different and inconsistent code, which threatens reliability and evaluation.

calismalar.baslik: SecurityEval Dataset: Mining Vulnerability Examples to Evaluate Machine Learning-Based Code Generation Techniques
calismalar.gerekce: It is one of the first CWE-based datasets for evaluating the security of generated code.

calismalar.baslik: Is Stack Overflow Obsolete? An Empirical Study of the Characteristics of ChatGPT Answers to Stack Overflow Questions
calismalar.gerekce: It found that 52% of ChatGPT's programming answers were wrong, and that users often missed these errors.

calismalar.baslik: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
calismalar.gerekce: It shows how far models are from producing correct code in real repository contexts, which motivates research on errors at repository scale.
